parts.title: The parrot who came to stay
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When my grandfather moved to a small flat last spring, he could not take his parrot with him. The landlord did not allow pets, and Pepper, who is thirty years old and bright green, needed a new home. My parents said that he could stay with us for a few weeks. That was eight months ago, and nobody has mentioned him leaving since.

At first, I was not happy about it. Pepper talks, and not only in a polite way. He copies the sound of the doorbell, the washing machine and my mother's mobile phone, so the whole family keeps running to answer things that do not exist. He also learned to say "Dinner's ready!" in my father's voice, which is very confusing when you are hungry.

However, I slowly began to enjoy his company. In the afternoons, when I came home from school, the house was always silent, and Pepper would shout "Hello, you!" as soon as he heard my key. I started to talk to him about my day. He cannot give advice, of course, but he is a very patient listener, and sometimes he says "Really?" at exactly the right moment.

Last week, my grandfather called to say that his new landlord had changed his mind about pets. He asked if we would like him to take Pepper back. My whole family said no at the same time, and my mother was the first.

questions.prompt: Why did Pepper come to live with the writer's family?
options: He had been ill for some weeks recently.
Her grandfather could not keep him.
His cage had broken at the flat.
Her parents had always wanted a pet.
questions.explanation: The landlord of the grandfather's flat did not allow pets, so Pepper needed a new home.

questions.prompt: What was the problem with the way Pepper talked?
options: He only spoke at night when everyone was asleep.
He talked only when the family was eating.
He said rude words to the visitors who came.
He copied sounds that confused the family.
questions.explanation: He copies the doorbell, the washing machine and phones, so the family run to answer things that do not exist.

questions.prompt: How did the writer's feelings change?
options: She enjoyed having a listener at home.
She taught him to talk to visitors.
She began to teach him new words.
She became angry with her father.
questions.explanation: She started to talk to Pepper about her day and appreciated that he was a patient listener.

questions.prompt: What happened when Pepper's owner phoned last week?
options: He offered to send Pepper's food.
He said he wanted to visit them.
He said he could take Pepper back.
He asked for a few more weeks of time.
questions.explanation: The grandfather said his new landlord had changed his mind and asked if the family wanted him to take Pepper back.

questions.prompt: How did the family react to the offer?
options: They asked to keep him for longer.
They argued about it for days.
They asked for more time to decide.
questions.explanation: They all said no at the same time, which means they refused straight away.

parts.title: Dogs that work
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Many people think that dogs are simply pets, but some dogs have a very serious job. Assistance dogs help people who have problems seeing, hearing or moving. [1] The training takes about two years, and it begins when the puppies are only a few weeks old.

At first, the puppies live with volunteer families. [2] They learn to walk calmly on a lead, to sit quietly in shops and to ignore food on the floor. These lessons are not easy for a young dog.

At about twelve months, the dogs move to a training centre. [3] For example, a dog may learn to open doors, pick up a dropped phone or press the button at a pedestrian crossing.

Not every puppy passes the course. [4] Some are too nervous, and others find it hard to stay calm near traffic. These dogs are not failures: most of them find loving homes as family pets.

When a dog finally meets its new owner, the first meeting is often emotional. [5] "It changed my life," says one owner. "I go out on my own now."
sentences: Some dogs also work for the police.
Their job is to give the dogs experience of everyday life.
These clever animals are trained to be calm and to obey many commands.
The dogs must also like working and be happy to learn.
Within weeks, the two usually become a close team.
Trainers teach them useful tasks that match each owner's needs.
Their owners must pay for the food and for the vet.
Police dogs usually wear a special jacket with a badge.

gaps.explanation: "Assistance dogs help people..." leads to sentence F, which explains how the dogs are trained to be calm and obey commands; the next sentence is about the training.
"The puppies live with volunteer families" is followed by their job: to learn about everyday life, which links to the lessons that follow.
"The dogs move to a training centre" leads to trainers teaching useful tasks; the next sentence begins "For example".
"Not every puppy passes" continues with other conditions: the dog must like the work, and the next sentence gives reasons why some do not.
The first meeting with the owner is followed by what happens within weeks, and then by the owner's comment on how it changed life.

parts.title: Why do cats purr?
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Most people believe that cats purr when they are happy, and that is often [1]. A cat that is lying on your knee and feels safe will usually purr. However, cats also purr in other situations. Vets have noticed that some cats purr when they are in [2], or even when they are afraid. Scientists think that purring may help cats to feel better, because the gentle sound [3] a kind of comfort. Mother cats purr to guide their kittens, which are born blind and cannot [4] their mother's face. Many cats also learn to use purring to get what they want. They make a special, higher sound [5] they are hungry, and owners find it difficult to ignore. It is not [6] to tell what a purr means, but it is always interesting to listen.

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: "That is often true" confirms that cats purr when they are happy.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: Vets have seen cats purr when they are in pain; this fits the idea of comfort in difficult situations.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: The sound "gives a kind of comfort" means it provides comfort.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: Newborn kittens are blind, so they cannot recognise their mother's face.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: "When they are hungry" says the time that the special sound is made.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: The writer means it is not easy to understand the meaning of a purr.

parts.title: Thinking about a puppy
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage:
Dear Mum and Dad,
I know you said that we cannot have a dog, but please read this before you decide. I have looked [1] the shelter website, and there is a small puppy called Mochi who needs a home. I promise to walk him [2] day before school and to clean up after him. The garden is big enough for him to play [3], and he will be good company when I am alone. If you say yes, I will use my pocket money to buy [4] own food and toys. I have already asked Grandma, and she has offered to look after him [5] we are on holiday. Please think about it, [6] I will do anything you ask!
Love, Nico

gaps.explanation: We say "look at a website"; "on" is also possible with a website.
We play in the garden: the preposition shows the place.
The possessive adjective refers to the puppy: his food and toys.
"When we are on holiday" gives the time that Grandma will look after him.
"And" adds the promise to do anything they ask.

parts.title: Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: leocadia
turns.text: Hello, this is Leocadia Hart. I have an appointment for my cat Milo on Friday afternoon, but I’m calling to change it. He hasn’t eaten anything for two days and I’m really worried, so Friday is too far away. Your receptionist said there might be a free place this evening, but I can’t leave work before seven and you close at six. So I’ll bring him tomorrow, before I go to work, if there’s a space. Please phone me back on my mobile. Thank you.

question.prompt: When will the woman take her cat to the vet?
question.explanation: Friday is too far away and the clinic closes at six, before she leaves work, so she will bring the cat tomorrow before work.

turns.speaker: maren
turns.text: Guess what, Torvald! We finally got some pets for the children.

turns.speaker: torvald
turns.text: Great! Did you buy the goldfish that you wanted?

turns.speaker: maren
turns.text: I was going to, but a neighbour told me they are boring and die quickly. My brother offered us his cat and his dog, but we don’t have the space or the time for those two.

turns.speaker: torvald
turns.text: So what did you choose?

turns.speaker: maren
turns.text: A pair of rabbits. They’re from the farm shop, one white and one brown. They need company, so we couldn’t take just one.

turns.speaker: torvald
turns.text: The kids must be delighted.

question.prompt: What pets did the woman get?
question.explanation: Goldfish were her plan, but she heard they die quickly, and she had no space for her brother’s cat and dog, so she took a pair of rabbits.

turns.speaker: bettina
turns.text: Shall we take the dog out this afternoon, Cyprian? It’s lovely and dry.

turns.speaker: cyprian
turns.text: Yes, but where? The river path would be nice, though it’s still muddy after the rain, and Buster hates having wet paws.

turns.speaker: bettina
turns.text: True. And I don’t want to walk along the street again. The traffic is horrible and he pulls on the lead.

turns.speaker: cyprian
turns.text: What about the big green space behind the library? He can run there, with no cars, and we can walk around the lake as well.

turns.speaker: bettina
turns.text: Perfect. I’ll find his ball.

turns.speaker: cyprian
turns.text: I’ll bring a bag for the mess.

question.prompt: Where will they walk the dog?
question.explanation: The river path is muddy and the street has too much traffic, so they choose the green space behind the library, which is the park.

turns.speaker: odile
turns.text: Hello, everybody. This is a message for anyone near Maple Road. I have lost my dog. She is a small brown dog with white feet, and she wears a red collar. Her name is Bella. Some of the neighbours know her as Biscuit, but that’s the name of the cat next door, so please don’t be confused. And Rocket was our first dog, who died two years ago. Bella ran away at about five o’clock yesterday. If you see her, please phone me on the number on the lamp posts. There’s a reward for anyone who finds her.

question.explanation: Biscuit is the neighbour’s cat and Rocket was an earlier dog that died, so the lost dog is Bella.

turns.speaker: saskia
turns.text: Welcome to Paws and Claws, your friendly pet shop on Main Street. This week we have good news for everyone with cats, dogs or rabbits. Our big bags of pet food are the same size as always, and most of them cost the same as last month. But if you buy one bag, you can take a second bag home for half the price. That’s a saving of up to four pounds. It’s the best deal of the year, and it finishes on Saturday. Come and ask our staff for advice about the best food for your animal.

question.prompt: Why is this week a good time to buy two bags?
options: The bags are smaller than usual.
Cats and rabbits like them most.
question.explanation: The bags are normal size and the deal is not about the animals, but the second bag costs half the usual price.

turns.speaker: marguerite
turns.text: Evander, where shall we put the hamster’s cage? I have to decide today.

turns.speaker: evander
turns.text: Not in the bedroom, definitely. Hamsters wake up at night and run on their wheel. You won’t sleep.

turns.speaker: marguerite
turns.text: You’re right. How about the kitchen? There’s a warm corner by the fridge.

turns.speaker: evander
turns.text: It’s too hot when you cook, and she doesn’t like the smell of food. I’d put it near the front door, on that little table. It’s cooler there, and everybody walks past and says hello.

turns.speaker: marguerite
turns.text: Good idea. I’ll move the flowers.

question.prompt: Where will the hamster's cage go?
question.explanation: The bedroom is too noisy at night and the kitchen is hot and smelly, so the cage goes on the table in the hall.

turns.speaker: philippa
turns.text: Hi Casimir, it’s Philippa. Thanks for the invitation to the farm on Saturday. I’d love to go, but I’m afraid I can’t, and it’s not what you think. I’m not scared of the sheep any more, I quite like them now. And I can borrow my dad’s car, so the journey isn’t a problem. The real problem is my neighbour’s dog. She’s on holiday and I promised to look after Ruby the whole weekend, so I can’t leave her. Maybe next time. Speak soon.

question.prompt: Why can't the woman go to the farm easily?
options: She has to look after a dog.
question.explanation: She likes the sheep now and can borrow a car, but she promised to look after the neighbour’s dog all weekend.

parts.title: Understanding the main idea
parts.instructions: Listen to six short conversations and choose the best answer.

turns.speaker: winifred
turns.text: Lucan, look at my garden! The new plants are all over the path.

turns.speaker: lucan
turns.text: Maybe it’s the wind. Or the frost. Are the flowers dying?

turns.speaker: winifred
turns.text: No, they’re fine. And Mr Brown from next door has been very kind, he even gave me some seeds. But every morning I find holes in the soil and the roots are out. Yesterday I saw a big grey cat digging there.

turns.speaker: lucan
turns.text: Cats love soft earth. You could put some sticks on the ground.

turns.speaker: winifred
turns.text: I’ll try it tonight. I’m so tired of this.

options: A cat is damaging the garden.
question.explanation: The flowers are fine and the neighbour is friendly; the trouble is the holes made every morning by a big grey cat.

turns.speaker: henrietta
turns.text: Ptolemy, Max hasn’t touched his dinner for two days. I’m getting worried.

turns.speaker: ptolemy
turns.text: Maybe he doesn’t like the new food. We could go back to the old kind.

turns.speaker: henrietta
turns.text: I tried that this morning, and he still turned his head away. Before I do anything else, I want a professional to look at him.

turns.speaker: ptolemy
turns.text: I agree. Dogs can have a problem with their teeth, and we can’t see it.

turns.speaker: henrietta
turns.text: I’ll call the vet, Dr Wells, now. We aren’t going to give him away, of course.

turns.speaker: ptolemy
turns.text: Of course not! Ask for an appointment tomorrow.

question.prompt: What are they going to do?
options: Take the dog to a new home
question.explanation: Old food did not help and they do not want to give him away, so Henrietta wants an expert to look at him and will call the doctor for animals.

turns.speaker: octavia
turns.text: Leopold, I found a lovely horse on the internet. It costs two thousand pounds.

turns.speaker: leopold
turns.text: I know, you’ve talked about it for months. But have you counted the rest? The food, the vet, the stable. Your friend says she’d let us keep it at her farm, but she wants money every month.

turns.speaker: octavia
turns.text: I suppose so. And we’re always away at the weekends. Winter would be especially hard, with the snow and the dark mornings.

turns.speaker: leopold
turns.text: Exactly. A horse needs time every single day.

turns.speaker: octavia
turns.text: Then it’s not fair on the animal. Let’s go riding at the centre instead.

options: To keep a horse at a friend's house
To buy a horse in the winter
question.explanation: The cost, the weekend travel and the hard winter work all show it would not be fair, so they will not have a horse and ride at the centre.

turns.speaker: cordelia
turns.text: Did you watch the programme about birds last night, Bartholomew?

turns.speaker: bartholomew
turns.text: I fell asleep after half an hour. It seemed to last forever.

turns.speaker: cordelia
turns.text: Really? It was long, but I didn’t notice. I loved the part about the swifts that fly for ten months without landing. I understood everything, the narrator explained it well.

turns.speaker: bartholomew
turns.text: So you liked it.

turns.speaker: cordelia
turns.text: Yes! I’m going to the library tomorrow to look for a book. I want to learn more about them, because there’s so much to know.

turns.speaker: bartholomew
turns.text: Maybe I’ll watch the rest.

question.prompt: What does the girl think of the programme about birds?
options: It made her want to learn more.
question.explanation: She agrees it was long but did not mind and understood it; she wants to go to the library and find out more.

turns.speaker: rosalind
turns.text: The receptionist says dogs aren’t allowed in the rooms, but they can stay in the garden house for a small fee.

turns.speaker: anselm2
turns.text: How much is it?

turns.speaker: rosalind
turns.text: Ten pounds a night. That’s less than the kennel by the beach.

turns.speaker: anselm2
turns.text: I don’t want to leave Scout with the neighbour. She’s always forgetting to feed him.

turns.speaker: rosalind
turns.text: And other hotels are more expensive anyway, and further from the beach. I think we should book this one.

turns.speaker: anselm2
turns.text: Agreed. I’ll phone them right away, and ask for the room with the balcony.

question.prompt: What do they agree to do about the dog?
options: Book the hotel and pay for him
question.explanation: Leaving him with the neighbour is not a good idea and other hotels cost more, so they agree to book this hotel and pay the fee.

turns.speaker: tabitha
turns.text: You look exhausted, Ignatius. Did you work late again?

turns.speaker: ignatius
turns.text: Not this week, the deadline is finished. And I didn’t go out last night, so I’m not tired from walking.

turns.speaker: tabitha
turns.text: Then what happened?

turns.speaker: ignatius
turns.text: The puppy! She cried from midnight to five. I took her out into the garden, I gave her water, I even slept on the sofa next to her, and still she cried.

turns.speaker: tabitha
turns.text: Oh, poor you. It gets better in a few days, I promise.

turns.speaker: ignatius
turns.text: I hope so. I need a very strong coffee this morning.

options: She went for a long walk.
Her new puppy kept her awake.
question.explanation: The deadline is over and he stayed at home; the puppy cried from midnight to five and he could not sleep.

parts.title: A talk about a school zoo trip
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: speaker-1
turns.text: Hello, everyone. I’m Gideon, and I’ll be your guide on Thursday’s visit to Hillside Zoo. I know you were hoping to go on Wednesday, but the zoo is closed to visitors that day for repairs, so we’re going on Thursday instead. The coach leaves school at nine o’clock, so please arrive ten minutes early. Last time some of you were late, and we waited for half an hour. When we arrive, we’ll go straight to the penguin house, where you can watch the birds being fed. It’s the most popular part of the day, and it’s much better in the morning, when they’re hungry. We’ll see the monkeys afterwards, and I’ll tell you more about them while we walk. We’ll stop for lunch at twelve, near the picnic area. Bring your own lunch, because the cafe is expensive, and don’t forget to take your rubbish home. After lunch there is a talk about snakes. I know some of you hate them, and the lizards have a talk of their own tomorrow, but the snake keeper is so funny that I’m sure everybody will enjoy it. You may even be able to touch one! Now, the weather. It has been sunny recently, but the forecast says showers in the afternoon. You won’t need a hat or sun cream, but please bring a waterproof jacket. An umbrella is not a good idea in a crowd, because it could hurt somebody’s eye. Finally, the gift shop. You will have some free time at the end of the day. Most of the toys cost around ten pounds, which is a lot, so I’ll ask you to spend a maximum of five pounds. Postcards and pencils are cheaper. Any questions? No? Then see you on Thursday morning!

gaps.prompt: The visit to the zoo is arranged for a ___
gaps.explanation: Wednesday is not possible because of repairs; the trip is on Thursday.

gaps.prompt: Students must be at school before ___ o'clock to take the coach
gaps.explanation: The coach leaves at nine o’clock; people should arrive ten minutes earlier.

gaps.prompt: The first activity is watching the penguins eat in their ___
gaps.explanation: They go straight to the penguin house; monkeys are afterwards.

gaps.prompt: In the afternoon, a keeper gives a talk on a kind of reptile: ___
gaps.explanation: The talk is about snakes; the lizard talk is tomorrow.

gaps.prompt: Because of the possible showers, students should bring a ___ that keeps them dry
gaps.explanation: A hat and sun cream are not needed; an umbrella is not a good idea, so they bring a waterproof jacket.

gaps.prompt: The maximum amount of money for the shop is ___ pounds
gaps.explanation: Toys cost ten pounds but the limit is five pounds.

parts.title: An interview with a wildlife rescuer
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Perdita, you run a rescue centre for wild animals. How did it all begin?

turns.speaker: perdita
turns.text: I didn’t go to university to become a vet, I wanted to, but I couldn’t afford it. And no, there wasn’t a farm waiting for me from a relative, I’ve always lived in a small house with a garden. What happened is that I found a hedgehog in the road one cold November evening. It was hurt and I kept it in a box, and people started bringing me more animals.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: People often find young birds on the ground. What should they do?

turns.speaker: perdita
turns.text: The first reaction is to take it home and feed it, and everybody thinks bread is a good idea, but it’s dangerous for them. In most cases the baby is just learning to fly. Its parents are watching from a tree nearby, and they’ll look after it. So the best thing is usually to leave it alone, and walk away.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: When should people phone you?

turns.speaker: perdita
turns.text: Not just because it’s raining, or because it’s dark. Lots of animals are perfectly happy at night, and the weather doesn’t bother them. I’d say phone me when you see blood, or when the animal can’t move normally. If it’s hurt, then speak to us immediately, any time of day.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What is the hardest thing for you?

turns.speaker: perdita
turns.text: Cleaning the cages isn’t pleasant, but I’m used to it. Money is a worry, because we only have donations, but we survive. The hardest moment is the day that an animal I looked after for months goes back to the wild. I’m happy for it, of course, but I always cry in the car park, and then I need a cup of tea.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: You also have teenage volunteers. What is their role?

turns.speaker: perdita
turns.text: They’re brilliant. They don’t take donations from the visitors, we have a box for that, and they aren’t allowed to drive because they’re too young. What they do is feed the baby animals with tiny bottles every three hours, and they clean their little beds. It teaches them to be patient and gentle.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Summer is coming. Any advice for hot weather?

turns.speaker: perdita
turns.text: Yes, a simple one. Put a bowl of fresh water in the garden, in the shade. Birds, hedgehogs and foxes all need to drink. You don’t have to give them extra food, since they find plenty in summer. And keeping your own pets in the house all day is not necessary, just give them water and a cool place.

questions.prompt: How did Perdita start her rescue centre?
options: She trained as a vet at a big university.
She helped a hedgehog she found.
She inherited a farm from her uncle.
questions.explanation: She could not afford university and had no farm from a relative; she found a hedgehog in the road and kept it in a box.

questions.prompt: What does Perdita say about young birds on the ground?
options: They need to be taken home at once.
questions.explanation: Bread is dangerous, and it is better not to take them home; the parents are watching from a tree nearby.

questions.prompt: When does she ask people to phone the centre?
questions.explanation: Rain and darkness are not reasons to phone; she says to phone when the animal is bleeding or cannot move normally.

questions.prompt: What does she find most difficult?
questions.explanation: Cleaning cages and money are not the biggest worry; the hardest moment is when an animal goes back to the wild.

questions.prompt: What do the teenage volunteers do?
options: They help to care for young animals.
They drive the animals to the vet.
questions.explanation: Visitors give money to a box and the teenagers cannot drive; they feed the baby animals with bottles every three hours.

questions.prompt: What is Perdita's advice for hot weather?
options: Leave out a bowl of water
Give the birds some extra food
Keep all pets inside the house
questions.explanation: Extra food and keeping pets inside are not necessary; the simple advice is a bowl of fresh water in the shade.
